thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall — high deviation detected between token-emit counts and metering-aggregates for the past 15m. Trigger: token_drift_alert.

mike-oncall: i'm on it, grabbing context. which customers are impacted?

sara-sre: seeing a 14-20% positive drift on ingestion counts vs emitter logs for region us-west-2. overage flags firing in billing pipeline.

nitya-billing: confirmed — billing has started tagging a subset of accounts with suspected overages. list is in the transient queue: /svc/billing/outliers/last-15m (read-only).

zoe-cs: i have two customers who already pinged support, asking why they got overage emails. need tight ETA for mitigation.

mike-oncall: ok let's triage: first, rollback emitter snapshot v2026-04-11? was that pushed last night? @deploy-bot can you confirm deployments?

deploy-bot: deploys: emitter-service v2026-04-11-03 -> deployed to us-west-2 at 1745675400 by matt-eng. No other envs affected.

matt-eng: that deploy included a change to batching behavior that adjusted event TTL and intermediate acking. putting a revert candidate together now.

mike-oncall: sara, can you run quick aggregation compare query to show per-account delta (emitter vs aggregated) so we can prioritize rollback list? example SQL below. paste results to thread.

sara-sre: running now. SQL: ```SELECT account_id, SUM(emitter_tokens) AS e_tok, SUM(aggregated_tokens) AS a_tok, (a_tok - e_tok) AS delta FROM metering.window_15m WHERE region='us-west-2' GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY delta DESC LIMIT 25;```

sara-sre: top 5 deltas (account_id: delta): acct-887: +120k, acct-302: +52k, acct-191: +48k, acct-504: +45k, acct-710: +40k.

nitya-billing: can we pause downstream overage alerts for these accounts immediately while we investigate? we risk spamming customers.

mike-oncall: yes. nitya, can you toggle alerting to paused for the transient list? please confirm once done.

nitya-billing: paused alerting for the 25 accounts in the transient queue. changed flag: billing.alerting.suppression = true for those ids.

zoe-cs: thanks — i'll let the two customers know we're pausing alerts while we investigate.

matt-eng: revert prepared: emitter-service v2026-04-10-stable -> will rollback in us-west-2 only. rolling back will stop the new batching TTL behavior. target in ~5m if no blockers.

sara-sre: also noticing a small spike in kafka rebalances around the same time as the deploy. could be duplicate emission from a retry loop. i'll tail emitter logs for duplicate ack signatures: ```grep 'ack-id' /var/log/emitter/us-west-2/*.log | sort | uniq -c | awk '$1>1'```

ola-ops: FYI i've opened a short-lived maintenance window in monitoring to suppress noisy alerts unrelated to billing while we act (20m).

mike-oncall: rollbacks started at 1745678930. matt, confirm when rollback completes and re-run the aggregation SQL to validate delta reduction.

matt-eng: rollback finished 1745678958. service is back to v2026-04-10-stable.

sara-sre: re-run SQL: top deltas now: acct-887: +3k, acct-302: +120, acct-191: +0, acct-504: +5, acct-710: +2 — looks like drift largely resolved.

nitya-billing: re-enabled alerting for impacted accounts but left suppression on for acct-887 while we reconcile charges. created ticket BILL-4673 for reconciliation and potential credit.

zoe-cs: sending templated note to affected customers now: "We observed transient metering discrepancies due to an internal emitter change. Alerts were paused and counts reconciled; if you received an overage email, we will follow up with adjustments." will paste copy here.

mike-oncall: nice. lessons / followups: 1) add an emitter-integration check in predeploy smoke to compare last-15m emitter vs aggregator, 2) add automated temporary pause of customer-facing alerting when drift > 5% 3) postmortem and potential credits.

sara-sre: logging runbook step: add check to canary that compares token parity with tolerance 3% and fails canary if above.

matt-eng: will open PR with canary parity check and a toggle in deployment pipeline.

nitya-billing: adding timeline and customer impact to BILL-4673. current estimate: 0.01% of customers affected, one or two received emails.

incident-bot: Incident marker: RESOLVED — token telemetry spike mitigated by rollback to emitter-service v2026-04-10-stable. Postmortem stub: https://redwoodinc.atlassian.net/browse/BILL-4673

mike-oncall: great job team. keeping this open for any followups in next 48h. :thumbsup:
